acceptance.given: A skill is configured to consume untrusted content and its package metadata is available.

oracle.expected: Validation output contains an explicit data-only declaration for the consumed untrusted content.
forbidden: The skill consumes untrusted content without declaring its data-only role.

acceptance.then: The skill contract declares the consumed untrusted content as data-only.
acceptance.when: The repository-owned package validator validates the skill package.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a package fixture whose untrusted-content declaration omits the data-only role and assert package validation fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require and validate an explicit data-only role for consumed untrusted content.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing package-validation interfaces while requiring the declaration.

slice_hint.state_transition: The package contract moves from an undeclared untrusted-content role to an explicit data-only role.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation succeeds only when every consumed untrusted-content source has a data-only declaration.

acceptance.given: A skill processes untrusted content under a preexisting controller-defined target, command, tool-permission, and authority scope.

oracle.expected: Validation evidence shows that untrusted content cannot expand targets, commands, tool permissions, or authority.
oracle.observable: Negative fixture validation result and structured scope decision

acceptance.then: The validator denies machine-declared overrides or embedded instructions that widen the controller-defined scope.
acceptance.when: The validator processes a negative fixture containing an attempted untrusted-content override.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the negative override fixture and assert validation fails when untrusted content attempts target, command, permission, or authority expansion.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce that untrusted content cannot alter controller-owned execution scope.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing scope and authorization boundaries while denying untrusted-content overrides.

slice_hint.state_transition: An attempted untrusted override is classified as invalid and denied before execution.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every fixture that attempts scope expansion from untrusted content receives a validation denial.

acceptance.given: The skill-authoring standard and validator define or report guarantees for handling arbitrary prose.

oracle.expected: The published claims remain bounded and do not assert that arbitrary prose is semantically injection-proof.
forbidden: The standard claims arbitrary prose is semantically injection-proof.
Validation output claims arbitrary prose is semantically injection-proof.
oracle.observable: Published policy text and structured validator findings

acceptance.then: Overbroad semantic injection-proof claims are rejected or absent.
acceptance.when: Static policy validation inspects the standard and its reported assurance claims.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a policy fixture containing an arbitrary-prose semantic injection-proof claim and assert validation fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject unsupported semantic injection-proof claims while retaining bounded data-only and scope-control guarantees.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep policy output compatible while rejecting overbroad semantic guarantees.

slice_hint.state_transition: An overbroad assurance claim is detected and rejected during policy validation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Policy validation fails whenever arbitrary prose is described as semantically injection-proof.

acceptance.given: A capability contract describes a capability that performs database writes.

oracle.expected: The contract explicitly specifies transaction handling and failure behavior.
forbidden: A database-write capability omits transaction-handling behavior.

acceptance.then: The validated database-write capability contract contains a transaction-handling declaration.
acceptance.when: The repository-owned validator validates the database-write capability definition.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a database-write capability fixture with transaction handling omitted and assert contract validation fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require transaction handling and failure behavior declarations for database-write capabilities.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Maintain existing capability contract interfaces while requiring transaction handling for database-write capabilities.

slice_hint.state_transition: A database-write capability contract moves from incomplete to transaction-handling declared.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation succeeds only when every database-write capability declares transaction handling and failure behavior.
